query: How are the storage layer and search layer kept in sync after writes?

recall_results.summary: store/sqlite.rs writes go through a per-request connection model with WAL mode and FULL_MUTEX; commit happens before any side-index work begins.
Tantivy index refresh runs fire-and-forget after commit; writer-lock failure degrades gracefully into a skip and the next write retries the refresh.
usearch HNSW insertion happens in-process after commit; the dirty marker is only cleared on a full rebuild, not per-write, so partial-write races never leave a stale clean flag.
evidence_preview: dirty marker cleared only on full rebuild

recall_results.summary: The recall waterfall reads from all three sources without coordinating refresh timing: stale-by-a-few-ms reads are tolerated by canonical-first collapse and dedup at fusion time.

query: What runtime safety mechanisms guard the v0.23 resummerize path?

recall_results.summary: BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus 5-way CAS (claim token, snapshot updated_at, status-live) prevents a concurrent MergeInto from racing the rewrite write.
The 7-invariant Lossless Compression Contract validates every LLM rewrite before apply; a failure routes to the audit table without touching the canonical.
A 3-strike exhaustion fuse breaks the loop after repeated ContractViolation outcomes; ClaimLost and LlmError do not count toward the strike total.
Stale claim tokens older than 5 minutes are reaped so a worker crash mid-rewrite does not leave a permanently-stuck row.

query: How are LLM extraction, query expansion, reranking, and dedup verdicts kept from overloading the upstream provider?

recall_results.summary: extract/llm.rs hooks run on PostToolUse and feed an async queue so the editor never blocks on Gemini latency.
search/expand.rs query expansion fires its LLM calls in parallel with the original recall via tokio::join, so the user-perceived latency is bounded by the slowest leg.
search/rerank_llm.rs gates LLM rerank by a strong-signal bypass: if BM25 top-1 already exceeds the learned threshold, no LLM call is issued.
evidence_preview: no LLM call on strong-signal hits

recall_results.summary: extract/dedup.rs LLM verdict is only issued when lexical similarity falls in the ambiguous band; clear-merge and clear-distinct cases avoid the LLM entirely.
evidence_preview: LLM dedup verdict only in ambiguous band

recall_results.summary: v0.23.1 added a global LLM semaphore acquire_llm_permit() that bounds concurrent calls across all four code paths; default 8 permits.

query: How do M2 alpha learning, M3 survival decay, and M5 tiering all benefit from M4 HDBSCAN clusters?

recall_results.summary: M4 HDBSCAN runs nightly, materializing cluster IDs into the memories table; downstream subsystems read those cluster IDs as a stable per-memory tag.
evidence_preview: cluster IDs materialized in memories table

recall_results.summary: M2 alpha optimizer groups candidate-replay events by cluster ID and learns a separate CC alpha per cluster, so dense semantic regions can have different fusion weights from sparse ones.
evidence_preview: alpha groups events by cluster ID

recall_results.summary: M3 Kaplan-Meier estimator builds a separate survival curve per cluster; the per-cluster decay constant replaces fixed Ebbinghaus once enough events have accrued in that cluster.
M5 tier boundaries are computed per cluster: the t-digest streaming quantile estimator runs once per cluster ID so dense and sparse clusters get tier cutoffs appropriate to their distribution.

query: What rein subsystems use SQLite transactions and how do they avoid stepping on each other?

recall_results.summary: store_with_dedup wraps the lookup-then-insert flow in BEGIN IMMEDIATE so two concurrent stores of similar text cannot both create a new canonical.
ops/resummerize.rs uses BEGIN DEFERRED for the snapshot read and BEGIN IMMEDIATE for the apply write; the two phases bracket the LLM call cleanly.
ops/dedup.rs run_vec_dedup re-embeds and writes inside a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE so a concurrent reader never sees a half-applied vector update.
ARS Capability A concept-summary refresh wraps its read-then-CAS-write in BEGIN IMMEDIATE; the CAS detects a concurrent peer refresh and bails without writing.
evidence_preview: ARS Cap A wraps read-then-CAS in BEGIN IMMEDIATE

query: Where does the Neural Wiki GUI fit relative to the MCP server, REST API, and CLI surfaces?

recall_results.summary: Neural Wiki GUI lives under crates/rein/gui as a React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind app, built into static assets that rust-embed bundles into the binary under --features gui.
GUI talks to the rein server through 21 REST endpoints in mcp/rest.rs; auth is enforced by AuthPolicy middleware registered through the same A1 inventory mechanism as MCP tools.
MCP server in mcp/server.rs reuses the same OpsRuntime methods that REST endpoints call: every operation is authored once via #[op] and dispatched by all three adapters.
evidence_preview: REST endpoints call the same methods

recall_results.summary: CLI subcommands also adapt OpsRuntime methods through cli/, completing the trio of dispatch surfaces over the shared inventory.
